verdict.rationale: Sentry documents an Android SDK that automatically reports errors and exceptions, and supports Apple platforms through the sentry-cocoa SDK. It also handles debug information files so crash reports on iOS, Android and other compiled platforms get usable stack traces, and a community comment corroborates its Symbolicator work. The evidence never explicitly covers NDK/native-code crashes, and never describes the device, OS or app-version context attached to crash events, so the core is only partly shown. Missing for 10: explicit NDK/native crash capture, documented device/OS/app-version context on crash events, hands-on corroboration of mobile crash reporting.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture native mobile crashes — iOS, Android, NDK — with the device, OS, and app-version context needed to reproduce them

citations.quote: we get you up and running with Sentry's Android SDK, automatically reporting errors and exceptions in your application.
Sentry supports Apple platforms via the sentry-cocoa SDK.
Debug information files allow Sentry to extract stack traces and provide more information about crash reports for most compiled platforms.
It’s primarily used for managing debug information files for iOS, Android, release and source maps management
